question: Should OpenClaw solve memory-wiki vault isolation through a generic per-agent plugin config contract, a memory-wiki-owned vault routing contract, or a narrower ctx-template/CLI selector design?
rationale: The issue affects sensitive memory boundaries and persistent plugin state, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term config/API, SecretRef, validation, lifecycle, and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Design a generic agent-scoped plugin config contract
options.body: Add a shared `agents.list[].plugins` or equivalent contract with explicit merge precedence, SecretRef/redaction, schema validation, restart semantics, doctor behavior, and memory-wiki coverage.

options.title: Keep plugin config global and add memory-wiki vault routing
options.body: Leave `plugins.entries` global and give memory-wiki its own per-agent vault map or safe path-template contract, reducing generic core surface but making this a plugin-specific pattern.

options.title: Defer behind broader plugin isolation work
options.body: Treat per-agent plugin install/config/lifecycle as one larger design and keep this issue open as the memory-wiki security/use-case evidence for that design.

recommendation.title: Design a generic agent-scoped plugin config contract
recommendation.body: Add a shared `agents.list[].plugins` or equivalent contract with explicit merge precedence, SecretRef/redaction, schema validation, restart semantics, doctor behavior, and memory-wiki coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans repository config policy, plugin SDK boundaries, and security-sensitive memory isolation, and this owner is tied to those surfaces by CODEOWNERS and recent history.
